text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A dozen of left-wing Bulgarian intelectuals demanded the resignation of the Socialist cabinet over its flawed economic and social policy in a open letter to the Bulgarian Socialist party's Supreme Council and the party's parliamentary group. @

-- Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) plans to finalise in two weeks negotiations with the Agricultural Bank of Greece for investment of some $10 million by the Greek bank in Bulgaria's Bank for Agricultural Credit, BNB officials said.
-- The current spot price of Bulgarian wheat of $230 per tonne is among the highest price in the world, the Private bakers' union said.

-- The ruling Socialist party (BSP) will announce its position on a possible introduction of a currency board in Bulgaria by December 1 because the country's draft budget for 1997 will be largely dependent on that decision, a senior BSP official said.
The currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund pegs the national currency to a major currency to halt inflation and boost economic growth. @
-- Bulgarians have withdrawn currency deposits worth some $60 million from local commercial banks in October as a result of the current crisis in the banking sector, central bank figures showed.
-- The Sofia municipality might lease night service of some public transport lines to private companies, Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski said.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) officials will consult Bulgaria's commercial and official creditors on the possible introduction of a currency board in the country, a senior UDF official said.

-- A Bulgarian-Russian joint stock tobacco comany, based in the Russian town of Tver will start operation in December with an annual output target of 1,500 tonnes of cigarettes for the Russian market.
The joint venture was set up on July 1 with 51 percent of the capital owned by the Bulgarian cigarette maker Haskovo BT and 49 percent by Russia's Tverbank. @
-- Bulgarian commercial banks had 47.4 billion levs of overdue payments on refinincing from the central bank totalling 63 billion levs by October 25, BNB figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's opposition will seek a no-confidence vote in the Socialist cabinet because of the current economic crisis, Bulgaria's opposition Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov said.

-- A senior official from South Corea's Daewoo Corp. is in Bulgaria to discuss investment opportunities in the country. Daewoo was particularly interested in Bulgaria's state forklift truck producer Balkankar and the chemical maker Neochim, Bulgaria's Industry minister Lyubomir Dachev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
